items.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
items.summary: Hierarchical models have been proposed as synthetic settings for studying language. However, their relevance to realistic language corpora remains underexplored. In this work, we introduce tree-grams, autoregressive generative $n$-gram models that build the conditional probability tensor $p(x_n \mid x_{1:n-1})$ through a hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors. $n$ controls the maximal context window, whereas a rank hyperparameter $d$ controls model capacity, yielding an interpretable and systematically scalable family of approximators of language. We show how tree-grams outperform existing $n$-gram baselines, while remaining competitive with deep transformer-based language models. We demonstrate the utility of such controlled approximations by using tree-grams as generative models. In particular, we show that hyperparameter transfer under $μ$P can be made more robust when narrower models are tuned on simpler data, generated by tree-grams with moderate $n$ and $d$. In addition, we show that entropy and effective range of correlations control performance gap after fine-tuning. This is because tree-grams allow us to explicitly control horizon and capacity. When allowed to route across candidate topologies, we observe emergent sparsity in tree-grams. Such concentrated routing permits pruning upto 95\% of topologies without significant change in performance.
items.headline: Tree-gram Hierarchical n-gram Models as Controlled Language Approximators
items.brief: This work introduces tree-grams, autoregressive hierarchical n-gram models that build conditional probabilities via compositions of order-2 and order-3 tensors. Tree-grams control maximal context window and model capacity, outperforming existing n-gram baselines and competing with deep transformers. They enable explicit control of horizon and capacity, showing emergent sparsity and allowing pruning of up to 95% of topologies without performance loss.
items.why: Tree-grams provide interpretable, scalable approximations of language models with controlled capacity, relevant for understanding and designing efficient generative models potentially applicable to biological sequence modeling.
items.korean: 트리그램은 계층적 n-그램 모델로, 언어 모델의 용량과 문맥 범위를 명확히 조절하며 효율적인 생성 모델을 구현한다.

items.title: VRLLM: Turning LLMs into Powerful Tabular Classifiers
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on text, but whether pretrained LLMs are effective for large-scale tabular classification remains unclear, as many previous works demonstrate that LLMs' tabular data classification performance falls behind tree-based models or neural architectures designed for tabular data. At Visa Research, we managed to fine-tune a pretrained Llama 3.2 1B LLM on billions of rows of labeled tabular data and make it outperform a wide array of tabular classifiers and even our competitive production deep learning model. For ease of reference, we refer to the model as the Visa Research LLM (VRLLM). In this paper, we share how we achieved this exciting result, covering data preparation, training recipe, ablation studies of design choices and deployment validation. We also benchmark frontier LLMs on the same task and analyze their prediction behavior across model families and generations. Our interpretability experiments suggest that VRLLM learns feature-specific predictive associations, while component ablations indicate that the earliest two FFN layers contribute to the emergence of linearly decodable task information. Our paper provides an engineering recipe and a focused empirical case study on adapting compact LLMs to industrial tabular prediction tasks.
items.headline: VRLLM: Fine-tuning LLMs for Large-Scale Tabular Classification
items.brief: Visa Research fine-tuned a pretrained Llama 3.2 1B LLM on billions of labeled tabular data rows, achieving performance surpassing many tree-based and neural tabular classifiers. The study details data preparation, training recipes, ablation studies, and interpretability experiments showing feature-specific predictive associations. Early feedforward layers contribute to linearly decodable task information, demonstrating that compact LLMs can be adapted effectively for industrial tabular prediction tasks.
items.why: This shows that pretrained LLMs can be adapted to large-scale tabular data classification, a domain relevant for computational genomics datasets and biological feature matrices, expanding the applicability of foundation models.
items.korean: 사전학습된 LLM을 대규모 표 형식 데이터 분류에 성공적으로 적용하여 산업적 예측에 활용 가능함을 보였다.

items.title: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs
items.summary: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to reason over behavioral evidence, but existing LLM-based approaches to passive sensing have largely continued to rely on task-specific fine-tuning or sensor-specific pretraining. In this paper, we introduce OAK-Mind, a zerO-training, multi-Agent, Knowledge-grounded LLM pipeline for inferring mental health changes from passive sensing data. The pipeline organizes sensing data into behavioral dimensions including sleep, physical activity, location mobility, and smartphone use, and orchestrates specialized agents grounded in mental health literature to interpret longitudinal behavioral changes. It synthesizes their assessments and applies questionnaire-based symptom rating to infer changes relative to an individual's baseline assessment with human-readable rationale grounded in observed behavioral patterns and domain knowledge. Across datasets and prediction tasks, while without task-specific training, OAK-Mind achieves comparable or better performance than the most predictive supervised baselines trained on additional labeled samples. It also demonstrate consistent improvement upon direct prompting across four tested LLM backbones. Ablation analyses support the benefits of combining behavioral interpretation with symptom rating, distributing analysis across domain-specific agents, and incorporating domain knowledge. Our findings highlight the potential of knowledge-grounded, multi-agent LLMs for training-free inference of mental health changes from passive sensing data.
items.headline: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Multi-Agent LLM Pipeline for Mental Health Change Inference
items.brief: OAK-Mind is a zero-training, multi-agent knowledge-grounded LLM pipeline that infers mental health changes from passive sensing data without task-specific fine-tuning. It organizes behavioral data into dimensions like sleep and activity, uses specialized agents grounded in mental health literature, and synthesizes assessments with questionnaire-based symptom ratings. It matches or outperforms supervised baselines and improves upon direct prompting across multiple LLM backbones.
items.why: This approach demonstrates how knowledge-grounded multi-agent LLMs can perform training-free inference on complex behavioral data, suggesting potential for interpretable modeling of biological and psychological signals.
items.korean: 지식 기반 다중 에이전트 LLM을 활용해 훈련 없이 수동 감지 데이터로 정신 건강 변화를 추론한다.
items.evidence_note: Preprint status; results need further validation.

items.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
items.summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition. Following a quench to a free-fermion tight-binding chain, we uncover an unconventional dynamics in which the entanglement entropy decreases whereas the entanglement asymmetry increases, so that initially symmetric subsystems dynamically develop local symmetry breaking. This behavior is quantitatively captured by a quasiparticle picture describing the propagation of antipodal correlations. Our results reveal how symmetry-preserving dynamics can redistribute globally encoded symmetry-breaking coherence, making it locally accessible, and establish the initial entanglement structure as a key ingredient in determining the fate of local symmetries out of equilibrium.
items.headline: Symmetry Breaking Dynamics from Long-Range Entanglement in Crosscap States
items.brief: The study reveals that unitary dynamics preserving global symmetry can lead to local symmetry breaking when initial symmetry-breaking coherence is encoded in long-range entanglement of charge-deformed crosscap states. Entanglement entropy decreases while entanglement asymmetry increases after a quench, showing that symmetry-preserving dynamics can redistribute symmetry-breaking coherence to make it locally accessible.
items.why: This provides new insights into how entanglement structure governs local symmetry properties in quantum systems, relevant for understanding chromatin and epigenomic regulation via long-range interactions.
items.korean: 장거리 얽힘에 저장된 대칭 깨짐이 단위리 동역학에서 국소적으로 나타날 수 있음을 보였다.
items.evidence_note: Theoretical physics study; implications for biological systems are indirect.

items.title: Spectral Classification of Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
items.summary: We study the unscaled empirical singular spectra of deterministic skew Hilbert--Schmidt kernels evaluated on independent isotropic rows satisfying a uniform quadratic-form variance bound. For arbitrary varying kernels at spatial dimension $d$, tightness and collapse to zero are characterized by boundedness and vanishing, respectively, of the rescaled quadratic energy remaining after deletion of $\lfloor\varepsilon d\rfloor$ leading skew pairs, for every $\varepsilon>0$. A regularized positive-covariance detector proves the necessary direction without a spectral envelope and retains diffuse energy across arbitrarily many small modes. On this exact tightness class, a weighted deterministic source characterizes all probability limits of the empirical spectra through the classical canonical parametrization of symmetric freely infinitely divisible laws. For a fixed kernel, convergence of one bounded resolvent response to a positive deterministic limit, convergence of one normalized logarithmic determinant, and full empirical spectral convergence are each equivalent to a critical Weyl law; the limit is necessarily a possibly degenerate half-Cauchy law. Finally, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for polygonal Brownian Lévy-area spectra to recover the continuous-time bulk under arbitrary deterministic time partitions, even when the normalized mean-square matrix error diverges.
items.headline: Spectral Classification of Random Skew-Kernel Matrices via Free Probability
items.brief: This work characterizes the empirical singular spectra of deterministic skew Hilbert–Schmidt kernels evaluated on isotropic random vectors, linking tightness and collapse to quadratic energy conditions. It establishes equivalences between spectral convergence, resolvent behavior, and logarithmic determinants, identifying limiting laws as half-Cauchy distributions. The results apply to polygonal Brownian Lévy-area spectra and provide a framework for analyzing kernel matrices in high dimensions.
items.why: Understanding spectral properties of kernel matrices is crucial for analyzing high-dimensional biological data and chromatin interaction matrices, informing computational genomics and epigenomics methods.
items.korean: 무작위 스큐-커널 행렬의 스펙트럼 특성을 자유 확률론으로 분류하였다.
items.evidence_note: Mathematical theory; direct biological application requires further adaptation.

items.headline: New Sordoni Exhibition Explores Women’s Place in Art History
items.brief: The New Sordoni Gallery presents an exhibition focusing on the role and representation of women in art history, highlighting contributions and challenges faced by women artists across periods.
items.why: This exhibition sheds light on gender perspectives in art history, enriching understanding of cultural and social influences in fine art.
